sentences.text: Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 23.03.2021 passed in MVC No.1448/2019 by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Holenarasipura, (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners therein have preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 23.02.2019 at about 4.00 p.m. the deceased H.K. Shankara had stationed his auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-13/C-4481 for hire in an auto stand near railway station of Holenarasipura town, at that time, the tipper lorry bearing registration No.KA-06/D- 9183 being driven in a rash and negligent manner duly insured with respondent No.2 - Insurance Company, dashed against the auto rickshaw of H.K. Shankara, because of which, the said H.K. Shankara, died.
The petitioners are the dependants of the deceased.

4. Based on the pleadings and the evidence let in, the Tribunal concluded that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry and awarded compensation of Rs.12,09,000/- along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation to the petitioners.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners have preferred this appeal.
5. Admittedly, the accident is of the year 2019.
The petitioners have not established the income of the deceased before the Tribunal.
Hence, as per the chart prepared by the Lok-Adalath, the notional income to be taken for the year 2019 is Rs.14,000/- per month.
The deceased was aged about 45 years at the time of the accident.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121], a multiplier of '14' has to be taken.

entities.text: Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the law down by the Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680, 25% needs to be added to his income as future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Given the number of dependants, 1/4th of income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Thus, on the count of loss of dependency, petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.22,05,000/- (14,000 + 25% x 12 x 14 x 3/4).

6. Further, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644], there are five dependants and they are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium(Rs.40,000x5= 2,00,000).

entities.text:
New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Thus, in all, they are entitled to a sum of Rs.24,35,000/- as against Rs.12,09,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

7. Hence, the following:-
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
